summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by Pieria — by lot the bride of Periphas son of Egyptus when the sons of Aegyptus by Gorgo married the Pieria maidens at Argos; distinct from Actaea the Nereid daughter of Nereus.

story.text: Apollodorus lists Actaea first among the six daughters of Danaus borne on Pieria. The sons of Egyptus by Gorgo cast lots for them; Periphas drew Actaea. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom — Hyginus counts her among the brides who obeyed Danaus.
